chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no harm in hastening the Tawaf al-Hajj and the Tawaf of the women before the Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah before his departure to Mina. And likewise, there is no harm for one who fears an event that prevents his departure to Mecca from performing Tawaf and bidding farewell to the House, then passing through as he is from Mina if he is fearful.' And it is not permissible to precede the Tawaf of the women before the Sa'i. He narrated that.

key_terms.طَوَافُ الْحَجِّ: Tawaf al-Hajj (the principal circumambulation of Hajj)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When can the Hajj pilgrim perform Tawaf al-Nisa' and is it valid before Sa'i?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the flexibility in the sequence of Hajj rituals, permitting the early performance of Tawaf al-Hajj and Tawaf al-Nisa' on the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah to accommodate travelers fearing delays. It further establishes a specific jurisprudential constraint that Tawaf al-Nisa' cannot precede Sa'i, highlighting the structured yet adaptable nature of Shia fiqh regarding ritual timing and sequence. This ruling underscores the practical considerations of the pilgrim's state (khawf) while maintaining the integrity of the ritual order.
